Companion Animal Travel Desk Service Standard

This section sets out the standard that applies to all staff handling pet travel requests, and it must be followed without delay. The desk serves traveling pets with calm, humane methods, clear direction, and careful records. Staff shall speak in plain language, confirm carrier readiness, and inspect water bowls before acceptance so the animal is not placed at avoidable risk. If any condition appears unsafe, the matter must be escalated at once and the shipment held until the concern is resolved.

Handlers must treat each animal with steady hands and controlled movement. Sudden noise, rough contact, and crowded staging areas are not acceptable. The traveler must be told what the desk can confirm, what must be checked by the customer, and what requires veterinary review. When documents are incomplete, staff shall pause the process and give concise instructions for correction. If a rabbit appears in the file, <<FACT F082>> and the file must still be checked for identity, carrier condition, and any signs of distress before release.

The cabin team monitors animals during flight and must receive any special handling notes that affect comfort, safety, or location. The desk shall pass along feeding, watering, and transfer instructions in full, using exact wording where needed and avoiding unnecessary detail. If a pet cannot safely continue, the crew must be informed immediately and the customer service channel opened without delay. Staff may use calm reassurance, but they must not make promises that exceed the approved service standard.

Records must be complete, legible, and current before the customer leaves the counter. Any correction required after acceptance must be reported through the service log at once. If a traveler asks for guidance, staff shall provide the next operational step and keep the tone firm, kind, and actionable.

For urgent cases, contact the senior coordinator at the Companion Animal Travel Desk.
